reasons: The inserted sub-paragraph c cleanly delivers eight of the nine Vendor-side preferred elements: defence and indemnity for Customer and affiliates, IP infringement of the Hosting Services and deliverables, Vendor breach of law, Vendor-caused Client Content breach, gross negligence/wilful misconduct, and the notice/control/cooperation procedure.

Preferred fails on the remaining atomic element: the Customer-side indemnity in paragraph a is expressly left untouched and remains far broader than 'Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law' — it still covers any Client breach of the Agreement, System Agreement/Credit Repository defaults caused by Client's customers, and product/service injury claims 'whether or not defective'. The condition is present (a Customer indemnity exists), so the limitation was required and is absent.

Fallback is not an available alternative route: no usual exclusions (modifications, combinations, specifications), no procure/modify/replace/refund remedies, and no 3x annual fees super-cap were added.

Minimality is satisfied — a single concise sub-paragraph for an absent Vendor indemnity, with no hold-harmless padding, no extra indemnitees, no Customer defence duty, and no fallback remedies imported.
Intent is preserved: paragraphs a and b remain effective, and the inserted text uses only defined terms (Client, TrueLink, Hosting Services, Client Content).
To reach the locked preferred level, narrow paragraph a to Client Content and Client's violation of law (e.g., strike (i), (ii) and (iv) or limit them accordingly).
